info.title: TDEI Gateway Dev API
info.description: This is an API for interacting with the Transportation Data Equity Initiative (TDEI) system. It is intended for applications submitting data to and consuming data from the TDEI system. We currently support GTFS-Pathways, GTFS-Flex and OpenSidewalks (OSW) data schemas.

post.summary: Authenticates the user with the TDEI system.
post.description: Authenticates the user with the TDEI system using username and password. Returns an access token and refresh token if successfully authenticated. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used.

200.description: Authentication successful - Returns the access token for the user.

400.description: Password does not satisfiy with password policy.

401.description: Authentication failed - Check username and password.

404.description: User not found.

post.summary: Re-issue an access token
post.description: Re-issues an access token when a valid refresh token is sent to the server. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used. The `client_id` should match the client used when the original tokens were issued.

200.description: Successful validation of refresh token - Returns the refreshed access token.

401.description: Invalid or expired refresh token provided.

post.summary: Regenerates the API key for the user.
post.description: Regenerates the API key for the user. The old API key will be invalidated and a new API key will be generated.

200.description: Regeneration of API key successful - Returns the new API key.

401.description: Unauthenticated request. Check your access token.

get.description: Starts the Single Sign-On (SSO) login flow by redirecting the browser to the auth server authorization endpoint. The caller must supply a `redirect_uri` that is already registered as a valid redirect URL for the auth server client. After the user authenticates with the auth server, the auth server redirects the browser back to that `redirect_uri` with an authorization `code` and `state` query parameters. The frontend should then call `POST /api/v1/sso-login` with those values to complete login and obtain TDEI access and refresh tokens. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Frontend callback URL where the auth server will redirect after successful authentication. Must be registered with the auth server for the selected client.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Auth server client id used for the SSO flow. Optional; defaults to the configured default client id when not provided.

302.description: Redirect to the auth server authorization endpoint. Follow the Location header to continue the SSO login flow.

Location.description: Auth server authorization endpoint URL including client, redirect_uri, state, and other OIDC parameters.

400.description: Invalid redirect_uri. The provided redirect_uri is missing, malformed, or not registered with the auth server for the selected client.

post.summary: Complete SSO login
post.description: Completes the Single Sign-On (SSO) login flow by exchanging the authorization `code` and `state` returned from the auth server for TDEI access and refresh tokens. Call this endpoint after the browser is redirected back to the frontend `redirect_uri` from `GET /api/v1/sso-redirect`. The server validates the `state`, exchanges the authorization code with the auth server, and returns a `TokenResponse` that can be used with subsequent authenticated TDEI API requests. The returned tokens follow the same format as the username/password authenticate and refresh-token APIs.

200.description: Successful response - Returns access and refresh tokens.

401.description: Invalid code or state. The authorization code could not be exchanged, the state is invalid or expired, or SSO authentication failed.

get.description: Starts the Single Sign-On (SSO) logout flow by redirecting the browser to the auth server logout endpoint. The caller must supply a `redirect_uri` that is already registered as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the auth server client. After the auth server completes logout, it redirects the browser back to that `redirect_uri`. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used. The frontend should clear any locally stored TDEI access and refresh tokens after initiating logout.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Frontend URL where the auth server will redirect after logout completes. Must be registered with the auth server as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the selected client.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Auth server client id used for the SSO logout flow. Optional; defaults to the configured default client id when not provided.

302.description: Redirect to the auth server logout endpoint. Follow the Location header to continue the SSO logout flow.

Location.description: Auth server logout endpoint URL including client, post_logout_redirect_uri, and related OIDC logout parameters.

400.description: Invalid redirect_uri. The provided redirect_uri is missing, malformed, or not registered with the auth server as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the selected client.

get.summary: Lists the TDEI datasets in the system.
get.description:
This API returns filtered and sorted lists of TDEI datasets. The matching behavior of filter parameters may vary depending on the attribute type.

By default results will include all datasets in released status AND all dataset in pre-release status within the requesting user's project group. This behavior can be controlled by the status parameter. In no situation can a user see pre-release datasets from a project group the user is not part of.

Primary use cases include:
  • name search: Given a search string X, return all datasets with a name that contains the search string X
  • dataset id lookup: Given a tdei_dataset_id, return the dataset with the matching id
  • bounding box: Given xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, return datasets with dataset_area overlapping the bounding box
Sorting:

Users can sort datasets by 'valid_to', 'valid_from', 'uploaded date', 'project group name', and 'status'.

parameters.name: data_type
parameters.description: Type of the dataset. Filters datasets by matching the exact value from the supported enumeration.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status of the dataset: Filters datasets by status — All (default) returns released datasets and pre-release datasets from the user's project groups; Pre-Release and Publish return only datasets in that status from affiliated project groups.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Dataset name or title: Filters datasets where the name or title contains the specified search text.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Dataset version: Filters datasets using an exact match on the version value.

parameters.name: data_source

parameters.name: collection_method

parameters.name: collection_date
parameters.description: collection_date: Filters datasets collected after the specified date and time.

parameters.name: confidence_level
parameters.description: Confidence level: Minimum confidence level required. Returns datasets with confidence level greater than the specified value. Range: 0 (very low) to 100 (very high).

parameters.name: schema_version
parameters.description: Schema version: Filters datasets that match the requested data type schema version. The list of supported versions can be found at /api/v1/{data_type}/versions.

parameters.name: tdei_project_group_id
parameters.description: TDEI project group ID: Filters datasets that belong to the specified project group. Exact match.

parameters.name: tdei_service_id

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Bounding box: Specifies the geographic area to search within, using a bounding box defined by four coordinates in the order: west, south, east, north. Accepts an array of four numeric values.

parameters.name: other_published_locations

parameters.description: Dataset update frequency in months: Filters datasets based on how frequently they are updated. Uses a greater than or equal to match to include datasets updated at this frequency or more often.

This operation clones the datafiles in the dataset `tdei_dataset_id` to the designated project group `tdei_project_group_id` and service `tdei_service_id`, and uses the metadata file provided along with the API as the metadata. Returns cloned dataset id if the action is successful.

get.description:
Downloads the output file generated by the job.

Some jobs store other files beside their output, such as the Pathways-Convert job's per-level reference data. Pass `file` to download one of those instead.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: job_id uniquely represents the job request

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Path of another file the job stored, relative to the folder holding the job's output, for example `beacon_hill/reference/platform.geojson`. Path segments may contain only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, and may not start with `.`, so `..`, a leading `/` and backslashes are refused. Only `.txt`, `.json`, `.zip`, `.xml`, `.geojson` and `.md` files can be downloaded. Give the parameter at most once. With `file`, a Quality-Report job streams that file rather than redirecting to its report.

200.description: Successful response - Downloads the job output file

400.description: Invalid job_id, or a `file` path or file type that can't be downloaded.

401.description: Unauthenticated request. Check your access token.

404.description: Requested job not found, job download file not found, or the job has no such `file`.

post.summary: Upload a OSW dataset.
post.description: This endpoint enables users to upload an OSW dataset. The request must include the required parameters to complete the upload. The response includes a `job_id` for tracking the request.To check the request status, refer to the location header in the response, which provides the URL for the status API endpoint. By default, the dataset's status will be set to 'pre-release.' The dataset can be published using the `/publish` endpoint.

parameters.name: tdei_project_group_id
parameters.description: Project group id to which the dataset would be uploaded

parameters.name: tdei_service_id
parameters.description: TDEI service id associated with the above project group id.

parameters.name: derived_from_dataset_id
parameters.description: Dataset id from which this dataset was derived.

dataset.description: OSW file which is expected to be a zip file, internally has {nodes, edges, points}.geojson. If the extensions are present, then the zip file will have {nodes, edges, points}.extension.geojson files

metadata.description: Metadata information for the OSW dataset. This is a JSON file that includes details on how and when the data was collected, the file's valid dates, and other relevant information about the dataset. For more details, refer to the [metadata schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TaskarCenterAtUW/TDEI-osw-datasvc-ts/dev/schema/metadata.schema.json).

changeset.description: The changeset file records modifications to the sidewalk network included in the OSW dataset. It supports file formats with either .zip or .osc extensions.

202.description: The upload request has been accepted for processing. It returns a `job_id`, a unique identifier for the uploaded request, which can be used to track the status of the upload. The endpoint to check the status is provided in the `location` header of the response.

Location.description: Location api to find the status of request processing

400.description: The request's input parameters are invalid.

401.description: Unauthenticated request. Check your access token.

403.description: User unauthorized to upload the dataset.

404.description: derived_from_dataset_id, tdei_project_group_id or tdei_service_id doesn't exist in the system

post.summary: Calculates the quality metric on a dataset element tags
post.description: Calculates the quality metric on a dataset element tags for requested tdei_dataset_id. Tags are the specific attributes or characteristics relevant to the OSW data entity. For example entities like Footway, Crossing, and Sidewalk have tags such as surface, width, incline, and length, indicating attributes like the material, size, slope, and distance. Returns the tag quality metric for the dataset element tags.

parameters.name: tdei_dataset_id
parameters.description: Dataset ID for calculating the quality metrics of element tags.

file.description: OSW dataset element tag list. Example file format: [tag-quality.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TaskarCenterAtUW/TDEI-osw-datasvc-ts/dev/schema/tag-quality.json). OSW  tag schema definition [osw-tag-definition.json](https://github.com/OpenSidewalks/OpenSidewalks-Schema/blob/Audiom/opensidewalks.schema.json#L5)

200.description: Successful response - returns the tag quality metric for the given input parameters.

400.description: Empty tag list or unknown entity type or tag.

401.description: Unauthenticated request. Check your access token..

post.summary: Unions two OSW datasets into one, as the config directs.
post.description:
Combines two OpenSidewalks (OSW) datasets into **one new dataset**, as the request's `config` directs: which nodes to **snap** together, which duplicate edges to **dedup**, which kinds of way to **connect**, and how to merge zones and extension features.

The request returns a `job_id` straight away; the union runs in the background (see *Tracking the job* below).

**Nothing is implicit.** Every snap, dedup and junction comes from `config`. With no `config`, the output is the two datasets combined, unchanged. The 4.x parameters `proximity` and `entity_filters` are no longer accepted (see *Moving from 4.x*).

---

## 1. Dataset order

| Parameter | Role |
|---|---|
| `tdei_dataset_id_one` (**DS1**) | The default **anchor**: where a node moves or a duplicate is dropped, DS1's stays. |
| `tdei_dataset_id_two` (**DS2**) | Moved onto DS1 or dropped where it duplicates DS1; everything else is added. |

A snap or dedup rule can set `"anchor": "ds2"` to reverse this for that rule. Connect rules work in both directions. The two ids must be different datasets.

---

## 2. `config` — four sections

| Section | What it does | Modes |
|---|---|---|
| `snap` | Joins a DS1 node and a DS2 node of the same type within a distance; the non-anchor node moves onto the anchor node. | `off`, `default`, `custom` |
| `dedup` | Removes an edge that duplicates an anchor edge (whole edges only, never trimmed). | `off`, `default`, `custom` |
| `connect` | Makes junctions between two kinds of way: a node on one line (split there) and, across a gap, a short connector edge. Nothing moves. | `off`, `default`, `custom` |
| `extensions` | Merges zones and extension points, lines and polygons. | `off`, `default` |

- `off`, or the section left out: the stage does nothing.
- `default`: the published rule set (section 3) at the section's `proximity` (0.5 m when not given).
- `custom`: only the rules listed, in the order listed. **The first rule that matches a location takes it**; later rules skip it.

Stages always run in this order: snap → dedup → connect → stranding guard → zones and extensions → output.

---

## 3. Default rule sets

| Section | Rules, in order |
|---|---|
| `snap` | Nodes at exactly the same spot join, whatever their type (`coincident`); then `crossing`, `pedestrian`, `living_street`, `road` and `other` nodes each join their own kind within `proximity`. Anchor DS1, attributes `merge`. |
| `dedup` | `crossing`, `pedestrian`, `living_street`, `road` and `other` edges, each against its own kind: a duplicate when at least 80% of it (`min_overlap` 0.8) lies within `proximity` of an anchor edge and its direction is within 30° (`max_angle`) of it. Anchor DS1. |
| `connect` | `road-crossing` (crossing → road, `point`), `crossing-sidewalk`, `crossing-living-street`, `pedestrian-pedestrian`, `living-street-living-street`, `crossing-crossing` (all `geometry`), at `proximity`, without tags. |
| `extensions` | All four types enabled: points within 0.5 m, lines with 70% of their length within 0.5 m, polygons and zones covering more than 70% of the DS1 one. |

No default rule joins a road and a sidewalk, a sidewalk and a living street, or a crossing and a plain footway; add a custom rule for those.

---

## 4. Custom rules

### snap

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required | Which nodes the rule joins; both nodes must match. |
| `proximity` | the section's, else 0.5 | Maximum distance in metres, 0 to 5 (0 = the same spot only). |
| `anchor` | `ds1` | Which dataset's node stays put. |
| `attributes` | `merge` | `merge`: the anchor's values win and keys only the other node has are added. `anchor_only`: nothing is added. |
| `coincident` (section) | on in `default`, off in `custom` | Join nodes at exactly the same spot, whatever their type. |
| `others` (section, `custom` only) | none | Distance for node types no rule lists; left out, those do not snap. |

A pair of nodes is governed by the **first rule both match**.

### dedup

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | required | The kind of edge that can be removed. |
| `to` | required | The kind of anchor edge it duplicates (may differ from `from`). |
| `proximity` | the section's, else 0.5 | Width in metres of the corridor around the anchor edge (above 0, at most 5). |
| `min_overlap` | the section's, else 0.8 | Share of the edge's length that must lie inside the corridor (above 0, at most 1). |
| `max_angle` | the section's, else 30 | Degrees the edge's direction may differ from the anchor edge's (above 0, at most 90). An edge joining the same two nodes as an anchor edge is a duplicate at any angle. |
| `anchor` | `ds1` | Which dataset's edge survives. |

### connect

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | Unique within the stage; written on everything the rule creates. |
| `from` | required | Line A: the line whose end joins, or the line that crosses. |
| `to` | required | Line B: the line that is split. |
| `operation` | required | `point`: where A crosses B with no shared node, a node is made and both are split; an end of A that stops short of B gets a node on B and a connector. `geometry`: an end of A within reach of B gets a node on B (B is split there) and a connector to it; an end that crosses B and stops just beyond it meets B where it crosses. |
| `proximity` | the section's, else 0.5 | Largest gap in metres between A's end and B (above 0, at most 5). |
| `node_tags` | none | Tags written on the junction node the rule makes or reuses. Existing values win; a differing rule value is recorded in `ext:union_audit_<key>`. |
| `edge_tags` | none | Tags written on the connector edges the rule adds. |

Standard OSW keys in `node_tags` / `edge_tags` are written as given; any other key is written as `ext:<key>`. `_id`, `_u_id`, `_v_id`, `_w_id` and `ext:union_*` cannot be set.

### extensions

One block per type; every block and every key is optional.

| Block | Settings (default) | When enabled |
|---|---|---|
| `points` | `enabled` (true), `proximity` (0.5) | A DS2 point joins a DS1 point of the same type (same tags, ignoring `ext:*`) within `proximity`. DS1 values win; DS2-only keys are added; every DS2 value is kept in `ext:union_audit_<key>`. |
| `lines` | `enabled` (true), `proximity` (0.5), `min_overlap` (0.7) | A DS2 line with at least `min_overlap` of its length within `proximity` of a DS1 line joins it; DS2-only keys are added. |
| `polygons` | `enabled` (true), `min_overlap` (0.7) | A DS2 polygon covering more than `min_overlap` of a DS1 polygon's area merges into it (DS1 outline, DS2-only keys added); one that overlaps less is combined with it into one shape. |
| `zones` | `enabled` (true), `min_overlap` (0.7) | A DS2 zone covering more than `min_overlap` of a DS1 zone's area is dropped; the DS1 zone is kept. |

A type with `"enabled": false` keeps both datasets' copies. Disabling all four is rejected: use `"mode": "off"`.

---

## 5. Naming a type

The same way in every rule (`type`, `from`, `to`):

| Form | Matches when | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A built-in name | — | `"crossing"` |
| An object | every key matches | `{"highway": "footway", "footway": "sidewalk"}` |
| A list as a value | the key has any of the values | `{"highway": ["primary", "residential"]}` |
| `"*"` as a value | the key is present | `{"kerb": "*"}` |
| A list of the above | any of them matches | `[{"highway": "living_street"}, "sidewalk"]` |

Built-in names: `crossing` (`highway=footway` with `footway` crossing or traffic_island), `sidewalk` (`highway=footway`, `footway=sidewalk`), `pedestrian` (`highway` footway, pedestrian or steps, not a crossing), `living_street`, `road` (`highway` primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, service, unclassified, trunk or motorway), `other` (none of these). A node takes the types of the edges it lies on, plus its own tags (e.g. `barrier=kerb`).

---

## 6. Rules that always hold

Whatever the config, the union:

- never moves a kerb (`barrier=kerb`), and two kerbs join only at exactly the same spot;
- never moves anything twice: a node that moved is never a target for another;
- never joins lines on different levels (`layer`, `level`, `bridge`, `tunnel`);
- connects only across the two datasets; gaps inside one dataset are left as drawn;
- never splits a connector an earlier rule made;
- restores a removed duplicate when removing it would leave another edge hanging (stranding guard);
- removes an edge whose two ends are both on the anchor network only when the anchor edges inside its corridor already join those ends;
- drops nodes it left unused; nodes unused in the input are passed through.

---

## 7. Output

The job produces a zip with the six OSW files (`osw.nodes.geojson`, `osw.edges.geojson`, `osw.zones.geojson`, `osw.points.geojson`, `osw.lines.geojson`, `osw.polygons.geojson`) and **`union_report.json`**: the effective config (every default filled in), per-rule counts, warnings, input and output totals, and seconds per stage.

- **IDs:** nodes keep their stored ids; nodes the union creates get new ids above them. **Edges are renumbered.** `_u_id`, `_v_id` and zone `_w_id` lists refer to output node ids. Provenance tags carry the **original** GeoJSON `_id`s.
- **Added tags:**

| Tag | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ext:union_audit_<key>` | joined nodes, merged points, junction nodes | Every other-dataset (or rule) value that differs from the kept value, as `<original _id>-<value>`, comma-separated. |
| `ext:union_absorbed` | joined nodes; anchor edges | The original ids of the nodes that joined it, or of the duplicate edges it replaced. |
| `ext:union_confidence` | joined nodes, junction nodes, connectors | 1.0 at the same spot, falling towards 0 at the rule's distance. |
| `ext:union_rule` | junction nodes, connectors | The connect rule(s) that made or used it, in rule order. |

- Connectors also copy line A's `highway` and `footway`. Split edges keep their own tags.
- An `ext:*` key holding different JSON types on different features is written as text on all of them.

---

## 8. Validation errors (HTTP 400)

The config is checked before the job is created; the message names the section, rule and field (`rules[1]` is a stage's first rule). For example:

| Request | Message |
|---|---|
| `proximity` or `entity_filters` at the top level | `'proximity' is no longer supported: union 5.0 takes its settings in 'config' (sections snap, dedup, connect, extensions)` |
| The same dataset twice | `tdei_dataset_id_one and tdei_dataset_id_two must be different datasets` |
| `{"snapping": {...}}` | `Invalid config: unknown section 'snapping'. Allowed sections: snap, dedup, connect, extensions` |
| A connect rule without `operation` | `config.connect.rules[1].operation: is required — one of point, geometry` |
| `"from": "sidewalks"` | `config.dedup.rules[1].from: unknown type name "sidewalks" — use a tag match such as {"highway": "footway"} or one of crossing, sidewalk, pedestrian, living_street, road, other` |
| `"proximity": 9` on a connect rule | `config.connect.rules[1].proximity: must be greater than 0 and at most 5 (got 9)` |
| `"max_angle": 120` | `config.dedup.max_angle: must be greater than 0 and at most 90 (got 120)` |
| `"tags"` on a connect rule | `config.connect.rules[1].tags: a connect rule takes node_tags (for the junction node) and edge_tags (for the connector edge) instead of tags` |
| A setting next to `"mode": "off"` | `config.snap: mode off takes no other settings (got "proximity")` |
| `extensions.proximity` (flat key) | `config.extensions.proximity: each type has its own block now — use extensions.points.proximity (and extensions.lines.proximity)` |

Limits: snap `proximity` and `others` 0 to 5 m; every other distance above 0 and at most 5 m; `min_overlap` above 0 and at most 1; `max_angle` above 0 and at most 90; **at most 15 rules per stage**; rule names 1–64 characters without commas, unique within a stage; the whole config at most 64 KB. Unknown keys are rejected, never ignored.

---

## 9. Moving from 4.x

| 4.x | 5.0 |
|---|---|
| `proximity: p` | `snap`, `dedup` and `connect` each `{"mode": "default", "proximity": p}`, and `extensions` `{"mode": "default", "points": {"proximity": p}, "lines": {"proximity": p}}` |
| `entity_filters` edge filters | Custom snap, dedup and connect rules naming those types |
| `duplicate_buffer_width`, `duplicate_overlap_percentage` | A dedup rule's `proximity` and `min_overlap` (0–1, not 0–100) |
| line / polygon / zone overlap | `extensions` `lines.min_overlap`, `polygons.min_overlap`, `zones.min_overlap` (0–1) |

The defaults are close to 4.x, not identical: connect rules add connector edges instead of moving edge ends, and steps 4.x ran implicitly (such as road × crossing nodes) are now named rules listed in the report.

---

## 10. Tracking the job

The response is a `job_id`, and the `Location` header gives the status URL. Track the job with `GET /api/v1/jobs` (job type `Dataset-Union`). Once its status is `COMPLETED`, download the result with `GET /api/v1/job/download/{job_id}`. A failed job's message includes the reason.

UnionConfig.description: Union 5.0 configuration: up to four sections, each with a `mode`. A section left out is `off`; no config at all returns the two datasets combined, unchanged. A JSON string of this object is also accepted. At most 64 KB.

snap.description: Joins a DS1 node and a DS2 node of the same type within a distance; the non-anchor node moves onto the anchor node.

dedup.description: Removes an edge that duplicates an anchor edge (whole edges only).

connect.description: Makes junctions between two kinds of way. Nothing moves: a node is made on line B (B is split there) and, across a gap, a connector edge is added.

extensions.description: Merges zones and extension points, lines and polygons.

UnionType.description: Which features a rule applies to. A built-in name (`crossing`, `sidewalk`, `pedestrian`, `living_street`, `road`, `other`), a tag match (every key must match; a list value means any of the values; `"*"` means the key is present), or a non-empty list of these (any may match). A node takes the types of the edges it lies on, plus its own tags.

UnionTagMatch.description: Tag match: every key must match. A string value must equal the tag's value (`"*"`: the key is present); a list value matches any of its values.

UnionTags.description: Tags to write. Values are strings, numbers or booleans. Standard OSW keys are written as given; any other key is written as `ext:<key>`. `_id`, `_u_id`, `_v_id`, `_w_id` and `ext:union_*` cannot be set.

UnionSnap.description: `default` runs: coincident nodes join whatever their type, then crossing, pedestrian, living_street, road and other nodes each join their own kind within `proximity` (anchor DS1, attributes `merge`). `custom` runs only `rules`, in order; a pair of nodes is governed by the first rule both match. `off` takes no other settings.

proximity.description: Distance in metres, 0 to 5 (0 = the same spot only). Default for the section's rules; 0.5 when not given.

anchor.description: Which dataset's feature stays fixed. Default `ds1`.

attributes.description: `merge`: the anchor's values win and keys only the other node has are added. `anchor_only`: nothing is added. Differing values are always kept in `ext:union_audit_<key>`.

coincident.description: Join nodes at exactly the same spot, whatever their type. Default: true in `default` mode, false in `custom`.

others.description: `custom` only. Distance in metres for node types no rule lists; left out, those do not snap.

rules.description: `custom` only. At most 15. Custom mode needs at least one rule, `coincident` or `others`.

name.description: 1–64 characters, no commas, unique within the stage. Default `snap-<n>`.

type.description: Which nodes the rule joins; both nodes must match.

proximity.description: Maximum distance in metres, 0 to 5. Default: the section's `proximity`.

anchor.description: Which dataset's feature stays fixed. Default `ds1`.

UnionDedup.description: `default` runs one rule for each of crossing, pedestrian, living_street, road and other, against its own kind (anchor DS1). `custom` runs only `rules`; an edge is checked by the first rule whose `from` it matches. `off` takes no other settings.

proximity.description: Corridor width in metres around the anchor edge (above 0, at most 5).

min_overlap.description: Share of the edge's length that must lie inside the corridor (above 0, at most 1).

max_angle.description: Degrees the edge's direction may differ from the anchor edge's (above 0, at most 90). An edge joining the same two nodes as an anchor edge is a duplicate at any angle.

anchor.description: Which dataset's feature stays fixed. Default `ds1`.

rules.description: `custom` only, and required there. At most 15.

name.description: 1–64 characters, no commas, unique within the stage. Default `dedup-<n>`.

from.description: The kind of edge that can be removed.

to.description: The kind of anchor edge it duplicates (may differ from `from`).

proximity.description: Corridor width in metres. Default: the section's `proximity`.

anchor.description: Which dataset's feature stays fixed. Default `ds1`.

UnionConnect.description: `default` runs `road-crossing` (crossing → road, point), `crossing-sidewalk`, `crossing-living-street`, `pedestrian-pedestrian`, `living-street-living-street` and `crossing-crossing` (geometry), at `proximity`. `custom` runs only `rules`, in order; the first rule that matches a location takes it. Only DS1 × DS2 pairs are joined. `off` takes no other settings.

proximity.description: Largest gap in metres (above 0, at most 5). Default for the section's rules.

rules.description: `custom` only, and required there. At most 15.

name.description: Required. 1–64 characters, no commas, unique within the stage. Written as `ext:union_rule` on what the rule creates.

from.description: Line A: the line whose end joins, or the line that crosses.

to.description: Line B: the line that is split.

operation.description: `point`: where A crosses B with no shared node, a node is made and both are split; an end of A that stops short of B gets a node on B and a connector. `geometry`: an end of A within reach of B gets a node on B (B is split there) and a connector to it; an end that crosses B and stops just beyond it meets B where it crosses.

proximity.description: Largest gap in metres. Default: the section's `proximity`.

node_tags.description: Tags for the junction node the rule makes or reuses. Existing values win; a differing rule value is recorded in `ext:union_audit_<key>`.

edge_tags.description: Tags for the connector edges the rule adds (connectors also copy line A's `highway` and `footway`).

UnionExtensions.description: `default` merges each enabled type; DS1's feature is always the one kept. Every block and key is optional; a type with `"enabled": false` keeps both datasets' copies; disabling all four is rejected (use `"mode": "off"`). The 4.x-era flat keys (`proximity`, `line_proximity`, `line_overlap`, `polygon_overlap`, `zone_overlap`) are rejected.

points.description: A DS2 point joins a DS1 point of the same type within `proximity`.

lines.description: A DS2 line with at least `min_overlap` of its length within `proximity` of a DS1 line joins it.

polygons.description: A DS2 polygon covering more than `min_overlap` of a DS1 polygon's area merges into it; one overlapping less is combined with it.

zones.description: A DS2 zone covering more than `min_overlap` of a DS1 zone's area is dropped.

proximity.description: Distance in metres (above 0, at most 5). Same type means the same tags, ignoring `ext:*` keys; a point with no other tags matches any type.
Corridor width in metres around the DS1 line (above 0, at most 5).

min_overlap.description: Share of the DS2 line's length that must lie in the corridor (above 0, at most 1).
Share of the DS1 polygon's area the DS2 polygon must cover to merge into it (above 0, at most 1).
Share of the DS1 zone's area the DS2 zone must cover to be dropped (above 0, at most 1).
